userAgentParser.q1: What information does a User-Agent string contain?
userAgentParser.a1: A User-Agent string provides details regarding the client browser application, rendering engine, operating system platform, CPU architecture, and device form factor.
userAgentParser.q2: Can this parser differentiate human browsers from bots and AI scrapers?
userAgentParser.a2: Yes. The parser maintains signature patterns for search engine bots (Googlebot, Bingbot), social crawlers, and AI scraping agents (OpenAI GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, ByteDance ByteSpider).
userAgentParser.q3: Is my User-Agent string sent to any external server?
userAgentParser.a3: No. The parsing engine executes 100% locally inside your browser memory without sending data to external APIs.
userAgentParser.q4: What does RFC compliant mean for a User-Agent?
userAgentParser.a4: RFC 7231 specifies that HTTP user agents should begin with product identifier tokens (like Mozilla/5.0) and maintain clean token formatting without illegal characters.

bmiCalculator.aboutText: Body Mass Index (BMI) calculator utilizing Quetelet Index standards (kg/m²) with WHO adult classification categories, metric and imperial conversions, and healthy weight range estimations.
bmiCalculator.feature1: Exact biometric calculation supporting metric (centimeters/kilograms) and imperial (feet, inches, pounds).
bmiCalculator.feature2: World Health Organization (WHO) weight stratification from severe thinness to Class III obesity.

bmiCalculator.faq1Q: What is the mathematical formula for Body Mass Index?
bmiCalculator.faq1A: The Quetelet formula is weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared: BMI = weight (kg) / [height (m)]².
bmiCalculator.faq2Q: Does BMI distinguish between muscle mass and body fat?
bmiCalculator.faq2A: BMI is a population screening metric that does not directly measure adipose tissue; muscular athletes may record higher BMI values without elevated adiposity.
bmiCalculator.faq3Q: What are the WHO BMI thresholds?
bmiCalculator.faq3A: Underweight is below 18.5, Normal weight is 18.5–24.9, Overweight is 25.0–29.9, and Obese is 30.0 or greater.
bmiCalculator.faq4Q: Is my personal biometric data stored or sent anywhere?
bmiCalculator.faq4A: No, all calculations are executed entirely in your local browser runtime.

base64Encoder.faq1Q: What is Base64 encoding used for?
base64Encoder.faq1A: Base64 is an encoding scheme used to represent binary data in an ASCII string format, commonly used in email headers (MIME), data URLs, and API payloads.
base64Encoder.faq2Q: Does this tool support Unicode and emojis?
base64Encoder.faq2A: Yes, our encoder properly handles UTF-8 byte sequences so emojis, international alphabets, and special symbols are preserved without data corruption.
base64Encoder.faq3Q: Is my data sent to any remote server?

base64Encoder.faq4Q: Is Base64 the same as encryption?
base64Encoder.faq4A: No. Base64 is an encoding format for data transmission, not an encryption algorithm. It does not provide security or password protection.

ageCalculator.faq1Q: How does this calculator account for leap years?
ageCalculator.faq1A: The algorithm computes elapsed leap days dynamically by checking Gregorian calendar intercalary rules (years divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400), ensuring exact day counts.
ageCalculator.faq2Q: Can I calculate the age of an event or historical milestone?

ageCalculator.faq3Q: Is my birthdate recorded or stored?

ageCalculator.faq4Q: Why do total days differ from simply multiplying years by 365?

checksumCalculator.feature2: Dual Text and File Support: Calculate cryptographic digests for raw text strings or directly inspect local files

checksumCalculator.faq1Q: What is a cryptographic checksum used for?
checksumCalculator.faq1A: A checksum acts as a unique digital fingerprint for data. Developers and system administrators use checksums to verify that downloaded software, ISO images, or packages have not been corrupted or tampered with.
checksumCalculator.faq2Q: Are my files uploaded over the internet?

checksumCalculator.faq3Q: Which hash algorithm is recommended for security?
checksumCalculator.faq3A: SHA-256 or SHA-512 are strongly recommended for security verification. Legacy algorithms like MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken and should only be used for non-security data integrity checks.

colorConverter.faq2Q: Why is HSL favored by modern CSS developers?
colorConverter.faq2A: HSL (Hue, Saturation, Lightness) aligns with human perception, making it intuitive to adjust brightness, create hover states, or build theme palettes by varying lightness while keeping hue constant.
colorConverter.faq3Q: How does WCAG contrast ratio score work?

cronExpressionGenerator.aboutText: The Cron Expression Generator & Parser is an essential DevOps and backend engineering utility that translates between human-readable scheduling rules and standard POSIX cron syntax. Supporting standard 5-field crontabs (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) and 6-field quartz syntax, it explains schedules in plain English and calculates upcoming trigger times.
cronExpressionGenerator.feature1: Visual Schedule Builder: Build complex recurring schedules using intuitive dropdowns and selectors without memorizing syntax
cronExpressionGenerator.feature2: Human-Readable Schedule Translation: Instantly translates cryptic cron strings (like "*/15 0-6 * * 1-5") into clear English descriptions
cronExpressionGenerator.feature3: Upcoming Execution Timestamps: Calculates and previews the next scheduled run times to prevent scheduling mistakes
cronExpressionGenerator.feature4: Universal Platform Compatibility: Generates expressions compatible with Linux crontab, GitHub Actions, AWS EventBridge, and Kubernetes CronJobs

cronExpressionGenerator.faq1Q: What do the 5 fields in a standard cron expression represent?
cronExpressionGenerator.faq1A: From left to right: Minute (0-59), Hour (0-23), Day of Month (1-31), Month (1-12 or JAN-DEC), and Day of Week (0-6 or SUN-SAT, where 0 and 7 are Sunday).
cronExpressionGenerator.faq2Q: What does the asterisk (*) and slash (/) mean in cron?
cronExpressionGenerator.faq2A: An asterisk (*) means "every value" (e.g., every minute). A slash (/) specifies step increments (e.g., */5 in the minute field means "every 5 minutes").
cronExpressionGenerator.faq3Q: Can this expression be used in GitHub Actions?
cronExpressionGenerator.faq3A: Yes! GitHub Actions workflow triggers use standard POSIX cron expressions on the UTC timezone schedule.
cronExpressionGenerator.faq4Q: How do I specify run times only on weekdays?
cronExpressionGenerator.faq4A: Set the Day of Week field to "1-5" (Monday through Friday). For example, "0 9 * * 1-5" runs at 9:00 AM every Monday through Friday.

cspHeaderBuilder.faq1Q: What is a Content Security Policy (CSP)?
cspHeaderBuilder.faq1A: CSP is an HTTP response header that instructs modern web browsers which resources (scripts, images, stylesheets) are permitted to load and execute, mitigating XSS attacks.
cspHeaderBuilder.faq2Q: Why should I avoid "unsafe-inline" in script-src?
cspHeaderBuilder.faq2A: Allowing "unsafe-inline" lets attackers execute injected inline scripts via reflected or stored XSS vulnerabilities. Use cryptographic nonces or hashes instead.
cspHeaderBuilder.faq3Q: What is the difference between CSP and CORS?
cspHeaderBuilder.faq3A: CSP controls which origins a browser page can load resources from. CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) governs whether an external origin can read resources from your server API.
cspHeaderBuilder.faq4Q: Can I test CSP in Report-Only mode?
cspHeaderBuilder.faq4A: Yes. You can use the "Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only" header to monitor violations sent to a reporting endpoint without blocking resource execution.

It supports three distinct modes: finding the sale price given a discount percentage, reverse-engineering the original price from a discounted price tag, and calculating stacked promotional discounts (e.g., 20% off plus an extra 15% clearance). discountCalculator.faq2Q: Can I find the original price if I only know what I paid?

hashGenerator.aboutText: The Cryptographic Hash Generator is a high-performance, browser-based security utility for producing deterministic, one-way hash digests from arbitrary text or binary data. Supporting standard cryptographic hashing algorithms—including SHA-256, SHA-512, and legacy MD5—the tool operates directly within browser memory. It is widely used by cybersecurity engineers, developers, and system administrators for file integrity validation, password hashing analysis, and digital signature verification.
hashGenerator.feature1: Multi-Algorithm Simultaneous Hashing: Computes SHA-256, SHA-512, and MD5 digests concurrently in real time as you type
hashGenerator.feature2: 100% Client-Side Cryptography: Operates completely offline in local memory without transmitting sensitive text to external servers
hashGenerator.feature3: Cryptographic Standard Compliance: Adheres strictly to NIST FIPS 180-4 (SHA family) and RFC 1321 (MD5) specifications
hashGenerator.feature4: One-Click Hash Export: Clean hexadecimal lowercase digests with convenient one-click copy buttons for rapid clipboard transfer

hashGenerator.faq1Q: Can a cryptographic hash be decrypted back to the original text?
hashGenerator.faq1A: No. Cryptographic hashes are one-way mathematical functions. You cannot reverse or decrypt a hash digest back into plaintext; you can only verify matches by hashing candidate inputs.
hashGenerator.faq2Q: What is the difference between SHA-256 and MD5?
hashGenerator.faq2A: MD5 produces a 128-bit digest and is cryptographically broken due to known collision vulnerabilities, used primarily for legacy checksums. SHA-256 produces a collision-resistant 256-bit digest recommended for modern security standards.
hashGenerator.faq3Q: Is this hash generator safe for sensitive passwords and API keys?
hashGenerator.faq3A: Yes. All hashing algorithms run 100% client-side inside your browser engine. Zero input characters or hashes are ever sent over the internet.
hashGenerator.faq4Q: Does case sensitivity affect the generated hash?
hashGenerator.faq4A: Yes. Cryptographic hash functions exhibit the avalanche effect: even changing a single character or its case produces a completely different hash digest.

hmacGenerator.title: HMAC Signature Generator
hmacGenerator.subtitle: Generate secure Hash-based Message Authentication Codes (HMAC-SHA256, HMAC-SHA512, HMAC-MD5) instantly.
hmacGenerator.aboutText: The HMAC Signature Generator is a specialized cryptographic utility designed to compute Hash-based Message Authentication Codes (HMAC) compliant with RFC 2104 and FIPS PUB 198. By combining a shared secret cryptographic key with a message payload through an underlying hash function (SHA-256, SHA-512, or MD5), HMAC guarantees both data integrity and authenticity. It is essential for signing REST API requests (e.g., AWS Signature Version 4, Stripe webhooks, GitHub webhooks) and verifying message authenticity.
hmacGenerator.feature1: Standard Algorithm Selection: Supports HMAC-SHA256, HMAC-SHA512, and HMAC-MD5 with exact cryptographic adherence
hmacGenerator.feature2: Client-Side Key Isolation: Shared secret keys and private messages are processed strictly in browser memory, never sent over the network
hmacGenerator.feature3: Real-Time Live Calculation: Automatically recalculates signatures immediately upon modifying either the key, message, or algorithm
hmacGenerator.feature4: Hexadecimal Digest Formatting: Produces standardized lowercase hexadecimal signature strings ready for HTTP header authorization
hmacGenerator.step1Body: Input your shared secret key or API signing secret into the designated key field.
hmacGenerator.step2Body: Choose HMAC-SHA256, SHA-512, or MD5, and paste your JSON payload or request string.
hmacGenerator.step3Body: Review the resulting hexadecimal HMAC signature and click "Copy" to use in your API headers.
hmacGenerator.faq1Q: What is an HMAC and how does it differ from a regular hash?
hmacGenerator.faq1A: A standard hash (like SHA-256) only verifies data integrity. An HMAC incorporates a secret cryptographic key, ensuring both data integrity and proof that the message originated from a party holding the secret key.
hmacGenerator.faq2Q: Is my secret key safe when using this tool?
hmacGenerator.faq2A: Yes, completely. All cryptographic operations are executed locally in your browser using client-side JavaScript. Your secret key and message payload are never transmitted to any external server.
hmacGenerator.faq3Q: Which HMAC algorithm should I choose for modern webhooks?
hmacGenerator.faq3A: HMAC-SHA256 is the industry standard for modern webhooks (used by GitHub, Stripe, Shopify, and Slack) offering high performance and robust security.
hmacGenerator.faq4Q: Can HMAC signatures prevent replay attacks?
hmacGenerator.faq4A: HMAC itself verifies message authenticity. To prevent replay attacks, webhooks commonly include a timestamp in the signed payload and verify it against a short validity window.

htmlEncoderDecoder.faq1A: In HTML, characters like <, >, and & have structural syntactic meaning. If untrusted input containing these characters is inserted directly into a page without encoding, browsers may execute malicious scripts, resulting in XSS vulnerabilities.
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq2Q: What are the most common HTML entities?
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq2A: The five core XML/HTML entities are: < (<), > (>), & (&), " ("), and ' (').
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq3Q: Does this tool decode named entities as well as numeric entities?

loanEmiCalculator.subtitle: Calculate your monthly loan payment (EMI) for mortgages, car loans, and personal loans — with a full amortization schedule.
loanEmiCalculator.aboutText: The Loan EMI & Mortgage Amortization Calculator is a financial planning instrument designed to compute Equated Monthly Installments (EMI) for home mortgages, auto loans, student debt, and personal bank loans. Using the standard reducing balance compounding formula [P × r × (1 + r)^n] / [(1 + r)^n - 1], the calculator provides an exact financial breakdown: monthly repayment, total interest accrued, overall debt liability, and a complete year-by-year amortization schedule showing principal reduction.

loanEmiCalculator.feature2: Comprehensive Financial Breakdown: Instantly displays monthly payment, principal vs. interest ratio, total interest, and final payoff date
loanEmiCalculator.feature3: Detailed Yearly Amortization Schedule: Interactive schedule details annual principal paid, interest paid, and remaining balance
loanEmiCalculator.feature4: One-Click Loan Summary Export: Generates a clear, shareable loan summary ready for clipboard copying and financial planning

loanEmiCalculator.faq1Q: What is an EMI and how is it calculated?
loanEmiCalculator.faq1A: An Equated Monthly Installment (EMI) is a fixed monthly payment paid to a lender. It is calculated using the formula EMI = [P × r × (1 + r)^n] / [(1 + r)^n - 1], where P is principal, r is monthly interest rate, and n is total months.
loanEmiCalculator.faq2Q: How does the amortization schedule work?
loanEmiCalculator.faq2A: In early loan years, a larger portion of each EMI covers interest. Over time, as the outstanding principal decreases, an increasing proportion of the payment directly reduces the principal balance.
loanEmiCalculator.faq3Q: Can I use this for home loans and car loans?
loanEmiCalculator.faq3A: Yes. It is universally applicable to any fixed-rate amortizing loan including residential mortgages, commercial real estate, auto financing, and personal loans.
loanEmiCalculator.faq4Q: Is my personal financial information stored?
loanEmiCalculator.faq4A: No. All calculations run strictly in your local browser memory; no loan amounts or interest rates are saved on external servers.

It automatically identifies core networking parameters (Host, User-Agent, Content-Type, Accept-Encoding), detects caching directives (Cache-Control, ETag, Age), and highlights critical security headers (Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options). httpHeaderInspector.feature2: Security Header Identification: Highlights presence and values of vital defense-in-depth headers like CSP, HSTS, and CORS
httpHeaderInspector.feature3: Clean JSON & Table Export: Formats parsed headers into accessible tables with single-click JSON clipboard export
httpHeaderInspector.feature4: 100% Private Client Analysis: No network requests are made; analysis occurs entirely in browser memory on pasted text

httpHeaderInspector.faq1Q: What headers are most critical for web application security?
httpHeaderInspector.faq1A: Key security headers include Content-Security-Policy (CSP) to mitigate XSS, Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) to enforce HTTPS, X-Frame-Options to block clickjacking, and X-Content-Type-Options to prevent MIME-sniffing.
httpHeaderInspector.faq2Q: Can I parse both HTTP request and response headers?
httpHeaderInspector.faq2A: Yes. The parser recognizes both request headers (e.g., Authorization, Cookie, Accept) and response headers (e.g., Set-Cookie, Cache-Control, Server).
httpHeaderInspector.faq3Q: How does it handle duplicate headers?
httpHeaderInspector.faq3A: Per RFC 7230, headers with duplicate field names (such as Set-Cookie or Accept) are properly preserved and grouped rather than overwritten.
httpHeaderInspector.faq4Q: Does this tool inspect headers over live network connections?
httpHeaderInspector.faq4A: This tool is an offline parser designed for analyzing pasted header blocks without sending outbound HTTP probes, ensuring maximum security and zero firewall restrictions.

imageCompressor.faq2Q: What compression quality should I choose?
imageCompressor.faq2A: For most photographic and web graphics, a quality setting between 75% and 85% is ideal. It typically reduces file weight by 60% to 80% while retaining crisp visual details indistinguishable from the original.
imageCompressor.faq3Q: Why is WebP recommended over JPEG or PNG?
imageCompressor.faq3A: WebP is a modern image format developed by Google that provides superior lossy and lossless compression. WebP images are generally 25%–35% smaller than comparable JPEGs and PNGs at equivalent visual quality.
imageCompressor.faq4Q: Is there a limit on how many images I can compress?
imageCompressor.faq4A: There are no server limits or paywalls. You can process dozens of images at once, bounded only by your browser's local memory and processor capability.

imageFormatConverter.faq2Q: What happens to transparent backgrounds when converting PNG to JPEG?
imageFormatConverter.faq2A: Since the JPEG specification does not support an alpha transparency channel, transparent pixels are automatically rendered on a clean white background.
imageFormatConverter.faq3Q: Which image format should I convert to?
imageFormatConverter.faq3A: Choose WebP for the best combination of quality and small file size for the web. Choose PNG if you need transparent graphics or lossless icons. Choose JPEG for wide compatibility with older software and photography.
